By Jim Saksa

November 16, 2026

Updated: November 16, 2026							at 4:49 pm

A government watchdog organization has filed an ethics complaint against Aaron Reitz, the U.S. attorney for the Southern District of Texas who has publicly threatened Democratic senators with criminal charges over their promises to conduct oversight investigations into the Trump administration.

The Campaign for Accountability submitted a grievance to the State Bar of Texas Monday, saying Reitz’s threats against Sens. Richard Blumenthal (D-Conn.) and Elizabeth Warren (D-Mass.) may have violated the Texas Disciplinary Rules of Professional Conduct.

Reitz sent letters to the senators alleging that their public comments about accountability amounted to violations of two statutes that criminalize attempts to deprive an individual of their constitutional rights through conspiracy or governmental action under the “color of law.” Legal experts say those claims are specious.

“The Constitution’s Speech or Debate Clause bars the prosecution of members of Congress for legislative acts, including investigations, and neither statute Mr. Reitz invoked makes it a crime for a senator to ask questions of donors and corporations,” the Campaign for Accountability wrote in a press release accompanying the bar complaint.

Moreover, federal law “makes it a crime to deliberately obstruct a congressional inquiry ‘by any threatening letter or communication,’” the watchdog added.

The complaint alleges Reitz’s conduct “raises substantial questions whether” he violated four Texas state bar rules: one barring prosecutors from “threatening to prosecute a charge that the prosecutor knows is not supported by probable cause,” another prohibiting “means that have no substantial purpose other than to embarrass, delay, or burden a third person,” and four provisions that generally forbid lawyers from breaking laws or obstructing justice.

“Officials who hold prosecutorial power have long been tempted to abuse it for political gain.
